newsitem.title: GERMANY: Buba's Sievert sees timely EMU start.
newsitem.headline: Buba's Sievert sees timely EMU start.

text.p: Bundesbank council member Olaf Sievert said on Thursday he still expected Europe's currency union project to start on time but said it would be difficult for Germany to make the fiscal grade.
"I still expect the Euro to arrive punctually, but I will not speculate about the participating countries," he said in the text of a speech to be delivered at a news conference.
On Germany's chances of making the grade, Sievert noted that last week's tax estimates had shown "how large the budgetary holes which need to be filled will be."
"It will certainly be very difficult to close them in the light of the limited room for manouevre, which will be maintained in the coming months," Sievert said.

Sievert, who is also president of the state central bank for Saxony and Thuringia, added that one-off or creative measures aimed at meeting the Maastricht EMU entry criteria were not helpful for the single currency profect.
